audits.text:
## 351de765e33f

Version 3.0.0; generator SHA-256:
`66d645c4a56226a323d2a0cc738874003dd0053c206b659af07295dc5dbe4d23`.
Canonical normalized rule hash: `f074243a0544`.

**A351-1 — Reproduced lesson-teaching gap, not an incorrect reference label.**
The canonical rule sorts individual monochrome objects by size descending and
then top/left reading order, and recolors the second object cyan. A plausible
rival instead chooses the second-largest *distinct size*, resolving a tie in that
size by reading order; with all sizes equal it returns the input unchanged.
This rival fits all 3/3 available labeled canonical pairs (two demonstrations and
one labeled test). It fails the emitted largest-tie and all-equal profiles.

Exact medium seed-17 witnesses at indices 0, 6, and 7 are retained. Index 0 is a
canonical-644 control that the rival gets right; index 6 is `tie_largest_four`
(sizes 6,6,4,2), and index 7 is `all_equal_five` (3,3,3,3,3). All pass self_check.
Racket recolors the second six-cell object at index 6 whereas the rival recolors
a four-cell object. At index 7 Racket recolors one three-cell object while the
rival changes nothing. `verified.json` includes complete input and output grids,
not just these verbal descriptions.

The public `Catalog.generate` probe uses 5 train + 2 query, seeds 3000..3099,
100 independently seeded episodes per band, all starting at sample index zero.
Each band has 700 unique input hashes, no rejections and no self-check errors.

| Band | Rival survives all five demos | Unrefuted rival disagrees on a query | Lesson denominator |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| easy | 100 | 0 | 100 |
| medium | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| hard | 0 | 0 | 100 |

The easy seven-input prefix never reaches largest ties or all-equal scenes.
The medium prefix puts a largest-tie example at query index 6, after five demos
that do not distinguish the rival. The hard prefix includes the necessary
counterexamples in training. This systematic prefix behavior is not repaired by
simply increasing the number of seeds. Full per-episode accepted indices, profile
histograms, input/Racket-output hashes, and source identity are retained in
`checks/audit/351de765e33f/public_sampler.json`. The same seed range is used across
bands; do not interpret the cross-band results as wholly independent.

**A351-2 — Test-layout friction reproduced, not a generator semantic defect.**
Directly collecting `generators/351de765e33f/tests` from repo fails with
`ModuleNotFoundError: puzzle_generators.per_puzzle.351de765e33f` (exit 2).
No fixture was edited. Public `arcpuzzles.runtime.prepare_runtime` copies the
recorded mapping into `.review/audit-portable-351de765e33f`; the unchanged mapped
`tests/test_generator_351de765e33f.py` then passes **6/6** tests (exit 0).
Original/copy test hashes match. The earlier failure and portable success both
remain in `checks/audit/351de765e33f/`; `portable-tests.json` records actual cwd,
argv, test hash, generator hash, and runtime-manifest hash.

**No additional domain/label violation found in this bounded check.** All 2,100
publicly labeled inputs (700 per band, with possible cross-band repeats) passed
the target validator. This does not prove the Python rule mirror matches Racket
on every valid input, nor certify arbitrary disconnected same-color scenes.
The generator explicitly restricts objects to distinct colors and moats; that is
a declared curriculum boundary, not a newly reproduced violation here.

audits.text:
## 351de765e33f

**Reproduced distribution/lesson shortcuts; no incorrect generated reference label found.**
Audited version `3.0.0`, generator SHA-256
`66d645c4a56226a323d2a0cc738874003dd0053c206b659af07295dc5dbe4d23`.
Canonical rule SHA-256 is
`8fe462eadf998eb9aadcc0dc34c894eddc815accf8f7a368067318402125856a`;
whitespace-normalized SHA-256 is
`f074243a05448e70405cc0d4f91c2282f5c3fb689c880651293688bbec3e0865`
(`RULE_HASH=f074243a0544`). The target source was unchanged.

**New finding — the moat distribution admits an eight-neighbor colorblind shortcut that fails a public demonstration.**
A rival groups all nonzero cells into eight-connected blobs, ignores their colors,
sorts blobs by size descending and top/left, and recolors the second blob cyan.
Every emitted object is four-connected and the generator separates different
objects by an eight-neighbor background moat, so the rival has exactly the same
objects and outputs on the entire construction grammar. This is a source-level
equivalence argument, supported by **87/87 fresh Racket-labeled generated inputs**:
24 pinned profile draws (all eight profiles in every band, seed 48100, indices
0..7) and 63 inputs from nine public-API lessons.

The exact **8×9 canonical variant 0, train pair 1** refutes that shortcut. Its
monochrome sizes are 9/4/2; the four-cell red object and two-cell green object
touch diagonally. The rival merges them into a six-cell blob. Fresh Racket
recolors only the four red cells; the rival also recolors the two green cells at
zero-based coordinates **(7,6) and (7,7)**. This is legal labeled public task
data. It is outside the generator's declared moat grammar: `self_check` and the
public apply-domain check reject it with `objects must have a one-cell background
moat`. The same sole validator error occurs for all three canonical inputs.
Thus the finding is missing public-topology coverage, not acceptance of an
invalid generated label. A four-neighbor colorblind rival was also checked and
fits all three public labels; it is not the refuted rival reported here.

Exact input, actual Racket output, rival output, domain status, source identities
and the two differing cells are retained in
`checks/audit/351de765e33f/evidence_summary.json`. The full public apply receipt is
`checks/audit/351de765e33f/racket.json`; all 27 applications succeeded with valid
outputs and matching canonical rule hash.

**Existing finding re-reproduced — medium lessons first expose a largest tie in the query.**
The retained audit's second-largest *distinct size* rival fits all three canonical
labels. Fresh `Catalog.generate` runs used 5 demonstrations + 2 queries, no
overrides, start index 0, and seeds **48200..48202** in each band.

| Band | Lessons | Rival fits all five demos | Unrefuted rival fails a query |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| easy | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| medium | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| hard | 3 | 0 | 0 |

Medium index 6 is always `tie_largest_four` (6/6/4/2): Racket recolors the
second six-cell object while the rival recolors the four-cell object. All 63
inputs passed `self_check`, with no generator rejections and 21 unique inputs
per band. Exact lesson grids, labels, rival outputs and accepted sample indices
are retained in `checks/audit/351de765e33f/lessons.json`.

**Bounds and checks.** The public `task_tests` check with `--phase audit` passed
**6/6** unchanged tests. All 24 pinned generated outputs matched the Python
mirror, and Racket matched all three canonical labels. No full battery,
exhaustive seed/offset census, or universal label-correctness claim was made.
Actual argv, cwd, exits and relative evidence paths are in
`checks/audit/351de765e33f/commands.json`; the focused check receipt is
`checks/audit/351de765e33f/task-tests/result.json`.
